scientific_question: On the clean canonical ArcLLM-v1 runtime, is there any operator/workload surface that the host NPU can actually execute with a valid representation/transfer path and an Amdahl upper bound large enough to justify opening a bounded NPU implementation study, or is the opportunity blocked by capability mismatch, representation/transfer cost, or insufficient runtime share?

Amdahl_rules.ideal_zero_cost_speedup: provider_or_transfer_overhead_must_not_be_set_to_zero_for_final authorization unless only an optimistic ceiling is being reported
Amdahl_rules.note: A family below this ideal ceiling cannot authorize implementation regardless of NPU peak TOPS.

gates.G1_hardware_presence: NPU enumerates locally with operational driver state
gates.G2_callable_provider: at least one local user-space path can enumerate/target the NPU without modifying ArcLLM production runtime
gates.G3_representation_surface: at least one candidate family can be represented without per-token full-weight repack and with explicit activation/weight transfer semantics
gates.G4_amdahl_headroom: candidate family has ideal zero-cost speedup >=1.10 from exact-target evidence
gates.G5_transfer_feasibility: available evidence does not already make transfer/setup overhead exceed the candidate removable-time budget

outcome_classes.PASS_OPEN_BOUNDED_NPU_TRANSFER_STUDY: G0..G5 pass for at least one candidate family
outcome_classes.UNDERIDENTIFIED_NEEDS_PROVIDER_MICROPROB: G1..G4 pass but G5 cannot be determined without a bounded provider-level microprobe
